answer: A microfluidic protocol curbs Sybil attacks by binding agent identities to physical chemical reactions. Verifiers instruct nodes to mix droplets along a spiral channel, measuring the synthesized pigment spectrum to anchor each cryptographic key. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of consuming reagents and dedicating microfluidic hardware per identity rather than running virtual clones. However, ambient temperature shifts alter reaction kinetics, causing false rejections of honest agents.
